claim: The NeoReach / Influencer Marketing Hub Creator Earnings Benchmark Report was an open, self-selected survey distributed through the two companies' own commercial creator networks between March and April 2021, with over 2,000 respondents — the weakest possible sampling frame for population income estimates.
stance_target: The use of the NeoReach/Influencer Marketing Hub creator earnings figures as representative of creators generally
scope_conditions: Fielded March-April 2021; n = 'over 2,000'; recruited from NeoReach's and Influencer Marketing Hub's existing creator rosters, i.e. creators already commercially active enough to be on an influencer-marketing agency's list; no country composition disclosed
quoted_support: NeoReach and Influencer Marketing Hub put their expansive Creator network to use, sending out an open survey from March to April 2021 to collect info on the Creator Economy, Creator earnings and monetization channels

claim: NeoReach found 43% of surveyed creators earning over $50,000 a year and 70% working as creators full-time, versus Linktree's contemporaneous finding that only 34% were full-time and only 12% of those full-timers cleared $50,000 — a divergence of roughly an order of magnitude between two vendor surveys measuring the same quantity in the same year.
stance_target: The claim that vendor creator-income surveys converge on a consistent estimate
scope_conditions: NeoReach n>2,000 fielded March-April 2021; Linktree n=9,576 fielded 2021; both self-selected; the gap is attributable to recruitment frame, since NeoReach sampled an influencer-marketing agency roster while Linktree sampled link-in-bio tool users
quoted_support: Not even one percent of surveyed Creators make over $1M, but 43% make above $50k a year. That's definitely a livable wage.

claim: NeoReach reports that 4% of its respondents had over 10 million followers and that nearly half had followings of 100,000 or more, confirming the sample is drawn from the extreme top of the creator distribution rather than from creators generally.
stance_target: The external validity of NeoReach's creator income distribution
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH survey 2021; note the report labels creators with 100,000+ followers as 'nano-Creators', a nonstandard inflation of a term conventionally applied to 1,000-10,000 follower accounts
quoted_support: Only 4% of Creators ranked in the topmost Supernova tier, amassing over 10M followers. Almost half of those surveyed are categorized as nano-Creators and have followings of 100k or more.

claim: NeoReach's tenure-to-income data show earnings rising steeply with years active — 46% of creators earn over $20,000 annually after 4+ years, 51% of 4+ year creators earn over $50,000, and by year 6 only 17% earn under $20,000 — but because only surviving creators were surveyed these figures describe survivors, not cohort outcomes.
stance_target: The claim that creator income reliably improves with time invested
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH survey, n>2,000, fielded March-April 2021; cross-sectional by self-reported tenure; anyone who quit before year 4 is absent from the denominator, so the apparent tenure premium is confounded with survivorship
quoted_support: 46% of Creators earn over $20k annually once they've been online for four or more years. ... 51% of Creators who have 4+ years of experience make over $50k a year. ... Once you hit the six year mark, only 17% make less than $20k

claim: NeoReach reports that 77% of creators derive the majority of income from brand deals — over three times every other revenue source combined — directly contradicting Linktree's finding that 70% of creators earn under 10% of income from brand partnerships and 67% have never done a brand deal at all.
stance_target: The Linktree finding that brand partnerships are a marginal income source for most creators
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH 2021 (n>2,000, recruited from an influencer-marketing agency network, which selects for creators who do brand deals) versus Linktree 2021 (n=9,576, recruited from a link-in-bio tool user base); the contradiction is best explained by recruitment frame rather than by either survey being wrong about its own sample
quoted_support: 77% of Creators bring in the majority of their income from brand deals, 3x more than every other revenue source combined

claim: NeoReach reports no meaningful correlation between follower count and creator income, citing surveyed creators separated by half a million dollars in annual income but only 1,800 followers.
stance_target: The claim that audience size is a poor predictor of creator earnings
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH survey 2021; self-reported income; the illustration is a single pair of respondents, not a correlation coefficient
quoted_support: There's no real income to follower count correlation, with some surveyed Creators reporting half a million dollars in income difference but only 1.8k more followers

claim: The $104.2 billion creator economy market size that Zippia and numerous downstream sources cite originates in this NeoReach/Influencer Marketing Hub report, where it is constructed by adding a $13.8 billion industry valuation to venture funding totals rather than by measuring creator revenue.
stance_target: The treatment of the $104.2 billion creator economy figure as a measured market size
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH 2021; the figure is assembled from an $850 million seven-month venture funding tally, a $13.8 billion industry valuation, a count of 500+ startups, and an assumed analogy to gig-economy growth trajectories
quoted_support: That $850 million investment is responsible for the recent rapid growth of the Creator Economy. If you pair that with the overall industry size valued at $13.8 billion this year and hundreds of new startups, the total Creator market size can be estimated at around $104.2 billion.

claim: NeoReach found 72% of surveyed creators name Instagram as their primary content platform, with TikTok at 13% and YouTube at 9%, a platform mix that reflects influencer-marketing agency rosters rather than the overall creator population.
stance_target: The platform representativeness of vendor creator surveys
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH survey 2021, n>2,000; fielded when TikTok had been monetized for roughly a year
quoted_support: Though a presence on multiple platforms is the norm, 72% of surveyed Creators list Instagram as their primary content channel.

claim: NeoReach reports that 78% of self-identified full-time creators earn more than $23,500 annually, a figure Zippia later restated as applying to 'influencers' generally, dropping the full-time qualifier.
stance_target: The fidelity of statistics as they pass from vendor surveys to aggregators
scope_conditions: NeoReach/IMH 2021, applies only to the 70% of the sample who self-identified as full-time; Zippia's restatement as '78% of Influencers make $23,500 or more annually' removes that restriction
quoted_support: 78% of self-identified full time Creators make more than $23,500 annually
region: Undisclosed; $23,500 is a US wage benchmark
